requirements.text: The automated diagnostic tool detects and identifies faults in chillers and cooling tower subsystems of HVAC units using sensed data acquired from the unit, unit specifications, unit installation and configuration data, and unit operation data (such as schedules).
The tool will provide the user with a visual indication of faults, descriptive information concerning the faults and their causes, and suggested corrective actions.
The tool will store the results of diagnostics for subsequent retrieval and use.
The tool must provide a capability to manually input and edit “fixed” data, i.e., data that does not vary in real-time.
The user must have the capability to configure the tool for continuous diagnostic analysis over an indefinite period of time.

The tool must print screen images of diagnostic results and historical data at user request and must provide long term storage of diagnostic results and permit the user to supply metadata relevant to the results, e.g., location, HVAC serial number, model number, user name, date, etc.

The tool may provide the user the capability to adjust the sensitivity of the diagnostic algorithms to increase the probability of exposing typically undetected diagnostic events or concealing detected diagnostic events (including false detections).
The tool will be capable of obtaining sensed data from a variety of sources.
The tool shall input sensed data in real time from data acquisition devices and the HVAC unit under diagnosis.
The tool shall permit sensed data to be input from an electronic file, though not simultaneously with sensed data from external acquisition hardware.
Sensed data used in or supporting diagnostic analyses shall be saved to permanent storage.
Sensed data input to the tool shall be stored to permanent storage with a precision of three significant figures.
The tool shall monitor performance and operational parameters listed in Table 7 for chillers and cooling towers and identify the specific faults in the specific fault categories listed in the table.

All stored diagnostic data and configuration files must be encrypted at rest using AES-256 or equivalent, and access to stored data must be restricted to authenticated users based on their assigned roles.

The authentication mechanism must enforce a minimum password length of 12 characters, implement account lockout after 5 failed attempts, and store passwords using a salted cryptographic hash (e.g., Argon2 or bcrypt).
The system must maintain an immutable audit log of all changes to fixed data, including the timestamp, user ID, and the previous/new values for every modification.
The system shall retain diagnostic results for a minimum of 24 months, with a storage capacity requirement of at least 500MB per HVAC unit per year.
The diagnostic engine shall implement a data-gap handling policy where gaps exceeding 5 minutes trigger a 'Data Unavailable' status for the affected diagnostic interval.

The system shall process and display diagnostic results within 5 seconds of receiving a complete set of sensed data, and shall support a data ingestion throughput of at least 1000 data points per second.
The system shall render the diagnostic information window within 500ms of a user selection, regardless of the size of the historical dataset.

OPEN: The PRD mentions wireless interfaces and network communication but lacks requirements for secure transmission (e.g., TLS/SSL) of sensed data. - All data transmitted over network interfaces, including wireless, must be encrypted using TLS 1.2 or higher to ensure confidentiality and integrity of the sensed data.

OPEN: The PRD mentions 'real-time' data acquisition but does not specify the required sampling frequency or latency requirements for the diagnostic engine. - The diagnostic engine shall process incoming sensed data with a latency of no more than 5 seconds from the time of acquisition, supporting a sampling frequency of at least 1Hz.

OPEN: The PRD requires the tool to be 'capable of obtaining sensed data from a variety of sources' but does not define the interface protocols or error handling for connection failures. - The system shall support Modbus TCP and BACnet/IP protocols and implement an automatic reconnection strategy with a 30-second timeout for failed data acquisition attempts.

OPEN: The PRD requires 'long term storage' of diagnostic results but does not specify the retention period, the number of HVAC units to be monitored simultaneously, or the expected data volume growth over time. - The system shall support the concurrent monitoring of up to 500 HVAC units and provide storage capacity for at least 5 years of diagnostic history per unit.
